title: The Morning Brief: Ohtani throws, Scheffler chases, Witherspoon signed long-term
dek: Friday and Saturday brought progress reports across baseball, golf, and football: Shohei Ohtani took his first mound session in three weeks toward a potential return this season, Scottie Scheffler built a two-shot lead into the St. Jude final round chasing his first win since January, and Devon Witherspoon became the NFL's highest-paid cornerback with a four-year, $132 million extension.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Three sports produced significant developments: Ohtani's recovery timeline is accelerating toward competitive action, Scheffler faces a final-round test against his closest friend in golf while hunting a breakthrough victory, and Witherspoon's record deal locks Seattle's championship-core cornerstone into his prime years.
bottom_line: Friday and Saturday moved three separate narratives forward with concrete stakes: Ohtani's recovery window narrowed toward a two-to-five-day checkpoint for his next bullpen session, Scheffler enters a final round seeking to convert strong positioning into a victory he has not captured since January, and Witherspoon's record extension ties a cornerstone defensive asset to Seattle through his prime. Van Rooyen's suspension removes a forward from Melbourne's finals push, Hunt chases a fourth gold Sunday in the mixed relay, and Tarling's death in Portugal raises questions about course safety procedures that remain unresolved.
body: The arc of competitive recovery defined the morning's picture. In Los Angeles, Ohtani threw 35 pitches in a bullpen session Friday, his first mound work in more than three weeks following a July 3 left knee injury. Manager Dave Roberts expressed confidence the two-way star could pitch this season if progression continues, with another bullpen session expected within two to five days. If that session clears, the Dodgers' rotation could add a significant contributor in the final stretch.

In Seattle, the Seahawks locked in their championship defense by agreeing to a four-year, $132 million extension with cornerback Devon Witherspoon, making him the highest-paid at his position in NFL history. The 25-year-old three-time Pro Bowler has made the initial ballot in each of his first three seasons and became a cornerstone of last season's Super Bowl LX run.

Golf produced a final-round setup with history attached. Scottie Scheffler shot 2-under 68 Saturday to reach 13-under and hold a two-shot lead over Sam Burns and Sungjae Im heading into Sunday at the FedEx St. Jude Championship. Scheffler, the world No. 1, chases his first victory since January after five runner-up finishes and five other top-4 placements this year. Burns and Scheffler will pair together Sunday for the first time as true contenders, a dynamic loaded with history: Burns beat Scheffler with a long birdie putt in a playoff at Colonial in 2022.

Beyond North America, the calendar delivered moments of consequence and loss. Amy Hunt won her third gold medal at the European Athletics Championships on Saturday in the women's 4x100m relay and will attempt a historic fourth in Sunday's mixed relay, which would make her the first athlete in the event's 92-year history to claim four golds at one edition. In Melbourne, Jacob van Rooyen of the Demons received a three-match suspension for a swinging arm strike that knocked out Port Adelaide's Aliir Aliir during Saturday's match, removing a productive forward from Melbourne's roster during the finals run. In rugby union, Australia defeated Japan 56-17 in Townsville to secure three consecutive Test wins for the first time since 2024 under coach Les Kiss. And in cycling, NSN withdrew its development squad from the Volta a Portugal on Saturday, one day after the death of 19-year-old Welsh rider Finlay Tarling in a Friday incident when a car entered the race course going opposite the direction and struck him.
